Costa, arriving at the summit on Thursday, said all leaders needed to approach discussions with an “open mind, a constructive approach and a sense of compromise” as he called for the budget to be approved in a “timely” way, adding: “That means by the end of this year.”
The budget has to be agreed unanimously, but countries are deeply split. In one camp are the so-called frugals – net contributors to the EU budget such as Germany, the Netherlands and Sweden – which want to reduce the overall size and shift spending priorities to defence and competitiveness, rather than farm subsidies and regional funds.
In the other camp are 17 countries in southern, central and eastern Europe, which want to ensure the flow of EU funds to traditional policies and oppose cuts.
France sits in neither camp, but has vowed to protect the common agriculture policy (CAP), which benefits French farmers. Maintaining farm payments would make it harder for Le Pen to unravel the budget. On the eve of the summit, Macron said “not a single euro of the CAP must be withheld from France in the next European multi-annual budget”.
Le Pen welcomed press reports that Paris was pushing for increased agriculture spending, but said Macron’s position had “nothing to do” with defending French farmers. “The objective would be to dissuade us – if the French entrusted us with the responsibility to govern – from defending French interests in European budgetary negotiations” she wrote on X.

theguardian.com.title: Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos wins race to be next ECB president
theguardian.com.text:
Spain’s Pablo Hernández de Cos has been chosen as the next president of the European Central Bank, to succeed Christine Lagarde, after winning support from the EU’s biggest countries.
The economist and monetary policymaker will become the first Spaniard to lead the ECB, defeating his rival candidate Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.
EU diplomats agreed two other appointments to the ECB’s executive board on Thursday: France’s Laurence Boone and Germany’s Markus Brunnermeier. The trio of appointments was a package deal, after France and Germany converged on choosing Hernández de Cos, who is expected to keep the ECB on the same path.
Following the talks European Council president António Costa confirmed the three appointments, saying: “This will pave the way for the formal appointment of the new ECB leadership by the EUCO [European Council] in December.”
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, also confirmed: “A consensus emerged on the nominations to the European Central Bank.”
The Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, who faces elections this weekend that he is predicted to lose, celebrated the victory of Hernández de Cos and the presence of Spaniards in other big EU roles, by hailing “a Spain that is leading in Europe as never before”.
Spain’s former deputy prime minister Teresa Ribera is one of the European Commission’s executive vice-presidents, with responsibility for a vast portfolio spanning the green transition and EU competition policy. The former Spanish economy minister Nadia Calviño leads the European Investment Bank.
Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, will become the fifth head of the eurozone’s central bank since it was founded in 1998. He is expected to take up his position after Lagarde stands down in February, during a time of political change and economic pressure in the 21-country eurozone.
Europe is entering a big election year, starting with Spain’s elections this weekend, with national votes to follow in France, Italy and (non-eurozone) Poland. European economies are under growing pressure from fierce Chinese competition, US tariff threats and soaring energy prices that are driving up inflation, as well as high debt in several member states.
One of his biggest challenges will be reining in surging prices: inflation in the eurozone hit 4% last month, up from 2.1% a year earlier.
Hernández de Cos, who is now serving as general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, is seen as supporting lower interest rates to boost growth.
Market analysts are closely watching what Hernández de Cos might say about France, where an embattled minority government is struggling to pass a budget. French debt is forecast to hit 122% of GDP next year, more than twice the limit allowed under EU fiscal rules.
Arne Petimezas, the director of research at AFS Group Amsterdam, said Hernández de Cos, who “leans dovish”, was the “continuity candidate”. He added: “Don’t expect de Cos to turn a blind eye to France and its fiscal predicaments. No carte blanche: bond buying will remain contingent on austerity and a path towards a lower debt ratio.”
The ECB’s approach to the French debt crisis will come under intense political scrutiny, especially after calls from the French far-right presidential frontrunner, Marine Le Pen, “to ease the burden of interest rates”.
Hernández de Cos is seen as a central banker in the mould of Mario Draghi, the celebrated former ECB president and Italian prime minister, who is credited with stabilising the eurozone at a pivotal moment in the debt crisis. Matthew Ryan, at the financial services firm Ebury, said Hernández de Cos was “likely to place greater weight on growth, financial stability and fragmentation risk than Klaas Knot, the alternative candidate and a genuine hawk”.
“We do not expect his appointment to alter the near-term rate path. The president sets the agenda but is ultimately one voice on the governing council, and rarely overrides the consensus.”
The contest was set in motion less than a month ago when Lagarde, the ECB’s first female president, announced that she intended to leave her post nine months early to speak her mind about world affairs and confront “the misrepresentation of the truth”.
Macron, who played a decisive role in appointing Lagarde, a former French finance minister, said EU leaders had welcomed her “decisive leadership during her term in office”.
Hernández de Cos’s appointment must still clear the European parliament and the ECB’s governing council, but these steps are seen as formalities.

theguardian.com.title: US army calls detonation of bomb chemicals in Iowa a success after fears of toxic plume
theguardian.com.text:
The US army blew up the nation’s entire stockpile of lead azide, a chemical used to make explosives, saying the first checks show Wednesday’s controlled detonation in Iowa didn’t spread toxic dust to nearby homes and farms.
Earthen barriers were put up and foam and water were poured onto a pair of bunkers holding the 5 tons (4,500kg) of lead azide, and officials said those measures appear to have absorbed much of the blast.
The US Environmental Protection Agency air monitors were detecting no lead in the air around the Iowa army ammunition plant in Middletown, and an alert sent to cellphones late Wednesday afternoon said it was safe to resume normal activities. Fema also issued an all clear around the plant, the US army reported.
Still, government agencies and independent researchers plan to do extensive environmental testing for lead – a heavy metal that’s especially dangerous to children and pregnant women – in the weeks ahead on water sources, farms, homes and playgrounds.
The army said the safest option had been detonating the stockpile right away because it was degrading and might explode uncontrollably at any time as the weather got colder.
Some experts cautioned that it’s too early to know whether communities are in the clear.
But Maj Gen Eric Shirley, who led the army operation, said the risk was “reduced as close to zero as it’s absolutely humanly possible”.
Since the military announced and then delayed plans for the detonation over the past two weeks, residents and environmental groups have voiced concerns about potential health and environmental impacts and about a lack of information about what to expect.
The smoke after the blasts
An Associated Press reporter filmed the blasts from less than a mile away and upwind from the site. Following two loud booms around 9am local time, a pair of white plumes rolled high in the air before quickly dissipating.
The army attributed the smoke to the foam sprayed on the bunkers to tamp down any dust.
Bystanders who parked on the side of a road to watch came away unimpressed by the size of the explosion.
Burlington resident Tim Brandt said he wanted to feel the ground shake, but instead the detonation reminded him of the noisemakers that crack when thrown on the ground.
“It was nothing,” he told the AP. “It seemed like government put fear in a lot of people over nothing.”
The army scheduled the detonation for Wednesday because the winds were blowing to the south-west and away from populated areas including Burlington, a city of just under 25,000 people along the Mississippi River.
The two controlled blasts destroyed all 68 barrels and didn’t set off any secondary explosions, Shirley said.
More lead test results needed
Donald Trump posted on social media that the army did a “great job”.
Acting secretary of the army Adam Telle along with the Republican governors of Iowa and Missouri also said it appeared to be a success and that the explosion was well contained.
However, the final results aren’t in yet, researchers said.
The EPA’s air quality data was promising, said Andrew Whelton, an environmental engineering professor at Purdue University who has helped communities recover from chemical disasters. Yet he stressed that samples need to be tested in a lab to determine if people face health risks.
“This should take days to weeks,” Whelton said. “But what we may see is different guidance issued to different communities based on how far they are from the detonation area and whether or not they were upwind or downwind.”
Colin Wellenkamp, the executive director of the Mississippi River Cities and Towns Initiative, said water treatment facilities along the Mississippi and Missouri rivers will be testing periodically to make sure that there are no detectable spikes.
Safety concerns and weather condition delays
Government officials had encouraged residents closest to the site and in range of the plume to evacuate and others to stay indoors.
Schools not already closed for the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday canceled classes and many businesses closed. Some residents sealed their windows and doors as a precaution.
Doug Seyb, a livestock farmer from Donnellson, lives far enough away that he didn’t hear or feel the explosions. But he was still concerned about the accuracy of EPA air monitors.
“All of these cows are pregnant,” he said, “and we just cross our fingers that we don’t have deformed calves and stillborns.”
Army steps to quash the plume
A court ruling this week put the detonation, originally planned for last Friday, back on track. The army changed the date amid public backlash and to allow more time for safety measures and favorable wind.
The army set up “blast barriers”, with concrete and sand barriers two stories high. Ballistic gels, foams and water were added to absorb the dust.
Environmental groups who sued to halt the detonation said on Wednesday that legal action and public pressure forced the army to take more protective measures.
Had the blasts happened last week as planned, many safeguards along with clearer evacuation plans and expansive monitoring wouldn’t have been in place, they said.
“Iowa and neighboring states deserve a full accounting of why the situation was allowed to get to the point of crisis,” said Sarah Green, executive director of the Iowa Environmental Council.
Lead azide crystallizing
The stockpile was brought to Iowa from bases around the country in 2009, according to Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives. The lead azide was stored just in case the military needed to use it again.
During an inspection in March, staff at the ammunition plant found the chemicals had partially crystallized, making them sensitive to friction and cold temperatures and creating the risk of spontaneous detonation.
Some residents said the timing could have been better, given that it was the day before Thanksgiving, but they acknowledged it needed to be dealt with now. Others worried about the potential impact down the road.
“I don’t think lead danger goes away any time soon,” said Lucy Giehl, who lives nearby in West Burlington. “It seems someone might have thought about all of this a little sooner before it came to this.”

theguardian.com.title: Politician hosts 400,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state
theguardian.com.text:
It takes a brave soul to try to match the mythic opulence of the wedding arranged by the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani for his son Anant in 2024. Estimates of the cost for the months-long celebration ran to at least $600m, with world leaders and celebrities among those on the guest list.
Smaller fry though he is, Anant Singh, a legislator in India’s poorest state, Bihar, gave it his best shot on Wednesday, albeit in a rustic rural setting, for the nuptials of his daughter Shivangi Singh, and Rishikesh Kumar, an MBA student from Georgia State University in Atlanta.
About 400,000 guests were hosted across 2.5 hectares at the family home in the village of Nadawa – a staggering figure even by the standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings. Guests were treated to 500,000 pieces of traditional sweets, and a feast prepared by an army of 500 chefs and cooks, Singh’s confidant Munna Singh told Agence France-Presse. One thousand kgs of mutton were reportedly used for kebabs and curries. Six makeshift helipads were erected for VIPs flying in from across India.
Kumar arrived at the venue in sunglasses and waving an orange scarf in a convoy of 151 cars (Hindus consider uneven numbers to be lucky). Among the gifts for the groom was a Land Rover Defender.
The roads leading to the venue were so choked with cars before the wedding that one guest escaped the gridlock, The Times of India reported, by jumping on a tractor and driving across the surrounding fields.
Guests were also treated to elaborate flower arrangements featuring blooms imported from China, and a fireworks display.
Instead of a DJ for entertainment, Singh planned a horse race. Gatecrashers clambered up into trees and on to electricity towers to catch a glimpse of the race, but the chaos and tumult was so great it had to be cancelled at the 11th hour. Lying around somewhere amid the wedding detritus was the SUV that would have gone to the winner.
Singh is a controversial figure. Elected five times to the state assembly, he has 28 criminal cases pending against him ranging from murder and attempted murder to extortion and kidnapping. All the cases are listed on the website of the Association for Democratic Reforms, an NGO trying to improve governance and strengthen democracy. Singh denies any wrongdoing.
In a television interview before the wedding, he pooh poohed the idea that there was anything unusual about the scale of the wedding preparations. “I laid on exactly the same thing for my elder daughter,” he said.
India’s wedding season has just kicked off. Between now and 15 December, an estimated 5.2m weddings are expected to take place across the country.

theguardian.com.title: ‘I’m no longer a UAE official’: UN hopeful Lana Nusseibeh tries to shake off Sudan record
theguardian.com.text:
Lana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war.
It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association.
Labelled by many British NGOs and others as an apologist for war crimes, Nusseibeh is presenting herself as a skilled diplomat with the network to put the UN back at the centre of mediation, development and human rights.
“These are very geopolitical times,” she said in an interview. “You need a geopolitical secretary general, because the fact is these geopolitical ruptures are not going away. These fissures in the international system are not going to dissolve any time soon.”
Nusseibeh had a setback last Friday, when three permanent members of the UN security council, China, France and the UK, all voted to “discourage” her candidature. The UN’s electoral system requires that she secure nine positive votes from the 15-strong security council, and no discouragement from the permanent five (P5) before being recommended to the UN general assembly.
She has the backing of the US and Russia, and thinks her cause is not lost. “Sometimes, the use of the veto is tactical. Sometimes, it’s a holding position, sometimes it’s a leveraging position. There are a number of different theories”.
The centre of the resistance to Nusseibeh’s candidacy is probably London, and specifically the Foreign Office, the penholder on Sudan at the UN, and this may explain the UK political blitz.
When questioned about her role in Sudan, she asked that her candidacy be seen in the round, highlighting her role in forcing humanitarian aid into Gaza, her support for Afghan women and promoting interfaith tolerance.
“Like every candidate, I come from somewhere, but the independence of the incoming secretary general is the key to their credibility.
“I’ve taken a leave of absence from my role in [the] UAE government in order to independently campaign for this role. But I think that if I was secretary general, Sudan would be the litmus test of success for any incoming secretary because it’s such a horrific humanitarian crisis.”
The war in Sudan, which erupted in April 2023 after a power struggle between the military and the Rapid Support Forces, has displaced more than 14 million people and created one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises. Multiple regional powers, including the UAE, have backed different local proxies since the beginning of the conflict in an attempt to win influence and strategic resources.
The UAE has long been accused of supporting the RSF in Sudan, a charge repeatedly denied by Nusseibeh, who has publicly disputed the findings of UN investigators.
A UN panel of experts suggested last month that the UAE had supplied crucial support to the RSF.
Asked if she regretted dissembling during her time as a diplomat, by denying the UAE had armed the RSF, or her personal role in challenging the UN reports critical of the UAE, Nusseibeh said she regretted that “the Sudanese civil war had continued for so long”.
Nusseibeh added: “But I don’t think saying that is enough for the Sudanese people and the people in the surrounding countries where they’ve also felt the impact of this war, or for the victims of sexual violence and in this conflict, the atrocities committed in El Fasher without accountability, and the use of chemical weapons against the civilian population; all of these are a litany of suffering that has been inflicted on the Sudanese people.”
Asked if the UAE had been supplying weapons to the RSF in a breach of a UN embargo, she replied: “I’m aware of the allegations. I haven’t read the last UN panel of experts report, but I’m not going to comment as I’m no longer a UAE official. In this campaign, I am a secretary general candidate.
“As secretary general, I would fully back the findings of all UN panel of experts reports and I’m aware that I think several countries have been mentioned in various reports.”She later added: “I would call out countries that are supplying arms to any of the parties, including those in the RSF … this needs a process that requires accountability for atrocities that have been committed. That it needs to be a process primarily led by the Sudanese people.”
Nusseibeh said she was willing to take risks to mediate and to put UN values, expertise and its development toolkit at the centre of disputes. Her analysis of contemporary diplomacy was that the world had descended into a default setting of non-cooperation, and the UN needed to restate the case for collaboration between nations as being in the self-interest of everyone.
The UN had been missing from too many conflicts, she argued, and she would set up a mediation board to try to use the full UN toolkit, ranging from confidence-building measures to development to secure peace. “What’s missing is this idea of a secretary general that is a strategist and a mediator-in-chief that is looking at the sort of the blips on the dashboard of conflict and saying, ‘How do we deploy to have maximum impact for most effective use of resource and cost?’ Because resources are not going up, they’re going down. I mean, we’re looking at, since 2010, 40% increase in military spending. So we’re using a lot of hard power as countries and systems to deter, but it’s not actually working.”
That would require some prioritisation at the UN – it has 4,000 different open mandates.
Her intelligence and skills as a diplomat are not in question. However, her track record over Sudan is.
One critic said: “It is a very smart strategic play by the UAE that seeks autocratic capture, and then the asset-stripping of the UN and its standards. The UAE would end the UN’s role on climate. It would be a catastrophe.”
The next security council vote is on Monday. By then some of the backmarkers may have dropped out of the race. The diplomats of the P5 may also be clearer on the flexibility of their mandates, in which case the papal conclave may finally produce white smoke.

theguardian.com.title: China reserves right to take ‘necessary measures’ after Trump’s new tariff proposals
theguardian.com.text:
Beijing has said it reserves the right to take “necessary measures” after Donald Trump’s administration proposed new tariffs on goods from China and other major trading partners, triggering a global backlash.
Among the suggested levies on 14 major trading partners announced on Wednesday, China is potentially facing one of the biggest hits. It would face the highest capped rate of 20%, which in some cases will be stacked on top of other import taxes for a total rate of 45%.
“China urges the United States to correct its erroneous practices and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation,” the Chinese commerce ministry spokesman, He Yadong, said at a regular briefing. “China will closely monitor developments and reserves the right to take necessary measures to firmly defend its legitimate rights and interests.”
Brazil was also singled out in the announcement after trade talks stalled.
Brazil’s government said on Wednesday that “Brazil will not yield to this type of threat”, adding in its statement that the “unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the framework of the ongoing bilateral negotiating process”.
It voiced particular indignation at US proposals for higher import taxes for raw and refined sugar and a new 10% tariff on aircraft, a change that would hit Embraer, Brazil’s largest aircraft maker.
It added that Brazil would continue to negotiate “without ruling out the possibility of adopting retaliatory measures in response to the illegal and unjust imposition of tariffs on Brazilian products”.
The Trump administration said that the new tariffs would be consistent with trade deals that the US reached last year with dozens of countries. They are being imposed under a law that allowed the president to target countries the US had found to engage in unreasonable or discriminatory trade practices. Jamieson Greer, the US trade representative, told CNBC that many US trading partners had adopted “market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America’s manufacturing base”.
The Trump administration’s new tariff rates would be capped at lower levels ‌agreed under trade deals that have already been concluded or remain under negotiation.
The administration will seek feedback from affected industries and hold a hearing on 25 January, suggesting the final duties won’t take effect until February or March.
Trump met his counterpart, Xi Jinping, in Shenzhen last week but the escalation in tariffs will not be a surprise to China, Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group’s China team, told AFP news agency.
The US and China last year reached a trade truce but that is set to expire on 10 January 2027. Trump and Xi are expected to meet again in Miami on the sidelines of the G20 in December.
“It has become a pattern before every major top leader summit,” Wang said, adding that she did not think the new measures would derail relations between Washington and Beijing.
“Xi has a high incentive to keep bilateral relations stable leading up to the 21st (Communist) party congress in October 2027,”Wang said.
A spokesperson for China’s embassy in Washington rejected allegations that China was ‌a source of excess capacity.
“The so-called issue of ‘industrial overcapacity’ does not really exist and should not be used as a pretext for political manipulation,” the spokesperson said, urging the two sides to jointly deliver on agreements secured between Trump andd Xi.
Earlier, China’s foreign ministry restated its opposition while calling for the US to resolve the issue through dialogue. “A tariff war or a trade war serves no party’s interests,” said the spokesperson Guo Jiakun.
Greer told CNBC that the administration was proposing a “broad exemption” for $30bn worth of Chinese goods in line with the deal. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this – they know what we’re proposing,” Greer said. “I think a lot of this is baked in.”
Some US analysts criticised the duties as too weak to change China’s trade practices.
China “is a bigger source of excess production than the rest of the world combined”, said Derek Scissors, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute. Yet Wednesday’s proposal “barely raises existing tariffs on China and will make no difference to the country’s trade behaviour.”
The EU said it rejected the premise of new tariffs and expected the US to stick by a deal struck last year. “The EU and the US share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” said the European Commission spokesperson Olof Gill.
Vietnam’s trade ministry said it was working with the US to complete its trade deal as soon as possible and would coordinate with relevant US agencies.
It added it was “preparing and submitting rebuttal comments on the preliminary findings as well as on inaccurate submissions and allegations ‌made by interested parties”.
In response to the US announcement, the Indian government denied it had any structural excess capacity in any sector, adding that it remained committed to an early conclusion of a trade deal between the two countries. Greer has said the tariff on Indian imports would be capped at 17% if a trade deal was struck.
Taiwan was also earmarked for new tariffs but Taipei on Thursday said it was confident it would keep its existing 15% tariff rate.
Taipei and Washington signed trade deals in January and February of ‌this year, which secured preferential treatment for semiconductors and other tech products that account for more than 70% of Taiwan’s exports to the US.
Other countries and regions affected by the new tariffs include Bangladesh, ‌Cambodia, the EU, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland and Thailand.
Tokyo’s top government spokesperson, Minoru Kihara, said it was “regrettable that a proposed measure targeting Japan has been announced”.
Singapore’s government said it was “very disappointed” with the proposals and denied it was protecting its domestic market or subsidising manufacturing.
Trump’s latest round of tariffs may be here to stay despite the Democrats’ electoral sweep in the US midterms. Some Democrats will probably support some of the tariffs, particularly on China. Trump can veto any legislation that seeks to overturn the import taxes.
However, the Democratic senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who will take over the finance committee next year, said he would “use every tool at my disposal to end Trump’s tariffs chaos”.
He added: “This is another blatant attempt by Donald Trump to reconstruct his illegal global tariffs. Global overcapacity is a serious problem, but Trump’s unilateral price-hiking tariffs are not the solution.”
With Associated Press and Reuters

theguardian.com.title: Israel ‘officially sanctions’ torture of Palestinian prisoners to extract confessions, report concludes
theguardian.com.text:
Israel has institutionalised the use of torture to extract confessions from Palestinian prisoners, sometimes documenting abuse in official records or granting advanced approval for “special measures” in interrogation, according to a report from the Public Committee Against Torture in Israel (PCATI).
This dangerous practice risked leading to irreversible miscarriages of justice, as Israel moved to implement a racist new death penalty law that targets Palestinians, the report said.
PCATI examined 42 cases in which Palestinians filed complaints about the use of torture by Shin Bet interrogators over the last decade.
More than three-quarters said they confessed after the use of “torture or other illegal methods”, and one in 10 provided incriminating statements about other people under torture.
“When it comes to Palestinian detainees, the Israeli legal system officially sanctions torture as a tool for extracting confessions, regardless of whether the content of those confessions is true,” said Sari Bashi, the executive director of PCATI.
“Torture as a tool of interrogation is particularly egregious given initiatives to impose the death penalty in Israel for the first time since 1962.”
Over the years, in hundreds of testimonies, Palestinian detainees have consistently described interrogations employing extreme sleep deprivation, physical violence such as slapping and kicking, threats, sexual violence and being held in stress positions.
Some of this abuse is also laid out in the official records of Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security service. PCATI details the case of a Palestinian lawyer arrested in February 2019 who was subjected to extreme sleep deprivation.
During an interrogation period lasting 27.5 days, or 660 hours, he was questioned for more than 552 hours, an average of 20 hours a day, with one session lasting nearly 48 hours. Some of the remaining 108 hours were spent travelling to and attending detention hearings.
In a 1999 ruling, Israel’s supreme court explicitly prohibited sleep deprivation as a deliberate interrogation method. Despite this, the lawyer was convicted of involvement in shooting attacks based on information extracted during this period.
The state inspector for complaints about Shin Bet interrogations (Mavtan) ruled that the interrogations took place in accordance with procedures, PCATI said.
More than 1,680 torture complaints were filed between 2001 and 2024 with Mavtan. None have led to an indictment.
Other cases are indirectly documented in Israeli judicial records, although judges rarely accept testimony about torture of Palestinians, PCATI said.
In one case, a detainee’s false confession, made under torture, was used as evidence by prosecutors. The man was released after his lawyer presented proof that he was not present at the scene of the crime, PCATI said.
Sleep deprivation was the most frequently used form of torture in complaints examined by PCATI, but more than half included the use of stress positions and other forms of physical violence.
Israel is a signatory to the UN convention against torture, but its legal system has effectively codified the use of violence and abuse where it is deemed “necessary” to extract life-saving information, PCATI said.
In a “necessity interrogation” or “military interrogation”, Shin Bet officials torture detainees “after consulting with their superiors and following an internal procedure for documenting their decisions and conduct”, the report said.
“[A] supposedly narrow exception ballooned and developed into a sprawling system of legal and administrative exceptions that swallowed the so-called rule, enabling the use of violence while maintaining the appearance of prohibition,” it continued.
There is no publicly available information on the scale of “necessity interrogations” inside the Shin Bet, PCATI said. They are an urgent concern as Israel moves to end a de facto moratorium on the death penalty, which had stood since the 1962 execution of the Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann.
“The death penalty is always wrong, because it’s cruel, irreversible and negates the right to life. No one should be executed, particularly not in a system tainted by systematic violence,” Bashi said.
In March, the Knesset passed a racist law allowing the execution of Palestinians convicted of terror charges over deadly attacks, but not Jewish Israelis who commit similar crimes.
In the occupied West Bank, where Palestinians are tried in military courts, execution is now the default punishment for a defendant found guilty of deadly terror attacks.
The legislation drew fierce international criticism, including from the UN’s high commissioner for human rights, Volker Türk, who warned that it would constitute a war crime if enacted.
A separate law empowers a special tribunal to impose death sentences in cases arising from the 7 October 2023 attacks.
Even in rare cases where courts have excluded confessions obtained under torture, Israeli case law allows prosecutors to use information derived from them as evidence to secure convictions.
PCATI said that as detention conditions worsened after October 2023, rights groups documented a sharp rise in violence by Israeli prison guards and soldiers, including beatings, attacks with dogs, electric shocks, threats and rape.
At least 103 Palestinian detainees have died in Israeli custody since 7 October 2023. Of 10 postmortems reviewed by Physicians for Human Rights Israel, five showed signs of physical assault and six showed evidence of medical neglect.
The Israel Prison Service said “all prisoners are held in accordance with the law”. The Shin Bet and Israel’s justice ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Costa Rica bars entry to UN rapporteur over 'links to terrorist acts'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Costa Rica's government said Thursday, November 26, it had denied entry to UN rapporteur Francesca Albanese, who has accused Israel of genocide, because she was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts."
The UN special rapporteur on the Palestinian territories arrived Thursday at the airport serving the capital San José, to receive an honorary degree from the University of Costa Rica, a public university.
Albanese "is the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts," Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica's immigration authority, which falls under the interior ministry, said in a video posted on social media. "I hope this clears up any doubts and makes clear the threat this woman poses to national security," he added.
The rector's office at the institution, the country's most important and prestigious university, said in a statement that immigration authorities were "blocking" Albanese's entry and asked the government to explain the decision.
The government of Costa Rican President Laura Fernandez is a close ally of US President Donald Trump and has pursued closer trade ties with Israel since she took office in May. Last December, Albanese criticized a free trade agreement between Costa Rica and Israel and called for its ratification to be put on hold, prompting a rebuke from the government, which accused her of interfering in domestic affairs.
'Face consequences'
The United States, Israel's main ally, imposed sanctions on Albanese after she criticized Washington's policy on Gaza. "You see the face of empire the day you touch a nerve or cross its boundaries," Albanese wrote from the airport.
The university said it was awarding the honorary doctorate, which it grants annually to a prominent figure, in recognition of her "solid academic background, experience, publications and work exposing wrongdoing."
The Italian independent expert has faced harsh criticism from Israel and some of its allies over her longstanding accusations that Israel has committed genocide and other war crimes against Palestinians in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
Israel's ambassador to the United Nations, Danny Danon, welcomed Costa Rica's decision.
"Those who exploit their UN mandate to spread vile propaganda, legitimize terrorist organizations, desecrate the memory of the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust, and relentlessly vilify the US and Israel should face consequences," Danon wrote.
Albanese was appointed by the UN Human Rights Council in 2022 and like other independent experts, does not speak on behalf of the United Nations.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Why mayors play a key role in France's presidential election
lemonde.fr/en.text:
For them, elections are in the past: France's mayors were elected (or re-elected) in March this year and have just begun their six-year terms in office. And yet, the main election on the horizon, the 2027 presidential election, could not happen without them.
Some of them are running for the Elysée: Edouard Philippe, center-right mayor of Le Havre, Normandy; David Lisnard, right-wing mayor of Cannes; Karim Bouamrane, Socialist mayor of the Paris suburb of Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine; Fabien Roussel, Communist mayor of Amand-les-Eaux, in the North; and Nicolas Dupont-Aignan, far-right mayor of Yerres, in the Paris region. The rest are courted for their signatures, as presidential hopefuls need to gather 500 sponsorships from elected officials to qualify for the election, scheduled for April 18 and May 2, 2027.
Beyond that, mayors and other local elected officials could play significant political roles in the presidential election campaign.
Ten years ago, Emmanuel Macron, a senior civil servant and former investment banker who had never held an elected office, preferred to rely on his closed circle of devoted advisers, dubbed the "Mormons," rather than a network of local elected officials. In fact, throughout his 10 years in office, the president never truly managed to take local officials seriously. The gulf has only grown wider over the years, to the point that Macron has not set foot at the annual French Mayors' Congress since 2021.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
lemonde.fr/en.text:
US President Donald Trump said Thursday, November 26, he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week. Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine.
Trump's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which the two leaders issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war.
"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly," adding: "I really believe this is a strong possibility."
The statement did not specify which territories Trump meant – and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II. European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in NATO-member Poland last week.
In their joint statement on Wednesday, Trump and Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war."
In a notable contrast with Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the US leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint. Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida on Thursday, Trump said he was unsure if Putin would be coming to the G20 summit next month in Miami, but "but if he wanted to come, he certainly can."
'Deadlock'
Trump's tone appeared markedly different to when Trump met Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen last week, both face-to-face and together with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump warmly greeted Putin and called him his "friend" at the summit, renewing concerns in Kyiv and European capitals that he was once again pivoting towards the Russian leader.
Asked Thursday about the apparent firmer tone this week, he said: "I don't know if I was tougher. I mean, I think I'm the one that gave them the anti-tank busters, right?"
Trump often cites his approval of Javelin missile sales to Ukraine during his first term as saving the country from Russia's initial assault. The US envoys on the Ukraine war, Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and business friend Steve Witkoff, have been accused of a similar willingness to take Moscow's side. In an interview with the German MD Meets Podcast on Wednesday, Kushner said that Putin had "showed restraint" because he had "agreed not to use nuclear weapons."
Kushner also described the Russian leader, whom he has met several times, as a "grandmaster of politics" – while calling the Ukraine conflict "a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia." But he acknowledged that the issue of territory in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow remained a sticking point with Putin.
"What Steve and I have deciphered from having many, many hours with President Putin and from the Russian team, is that you know the territorial issue is right now a little bit of a deadlock," he said. And he warned against any downward spiral in the Ukraine war, saying "it won't take a lot of miscalculation for this thing to escalate massively."

lemonde.fr/en.title: Spain's legislative elections: Andalusia, a testing ground for the right and the far right alliance
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Every day, as children from well-to-do families leave school in their uniforms, María Luisa (those mentioned by first name did not wish to give their surnames) leaves her home and sits on a bench on Calle Asunción. The long pedestrian thoroughfare cuts through Los Remedios, an affluent neighborhood on La Cartuja, the island flanked by two branches of the Guadalquivir River in Seville, in southern Spain, that gained international recognition for hosting the 1992 World's Fair. Impeccably dressed, her handbag clutched in her lap, the elderly woman amuses herself by watching little boys in shorts and loafers and little girls in tartan kilts.
On Monday, November 23, this true Sevillian, 85, said she had been the victim of a "pickpocket" and brooded over her resentment toward a country that "is upside down." She is looking forward to the November 29 snap legislative elections to "throw out" Socialist Pedro Sánchez, whose government is "made up of a bunch of incompetents [who] line their pockets." She said with a sly smile that on Sunday she would vote "half PP [People's Party, conservative], half Vox [far right]." It was her way of admitting she would back the far right, without which Alberto Núñez Feijóo's PP risks falling short of an absolute majority in the Congress of Deputies.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Simon Abkarian to succeed Ariane Mnouchkine at Théâtre du Soleil in Paris
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Ariane Mnouchkine, 87, appeared distinctly troubled as she sat on a bench at the entrance of her theater, enjoying one of the last rays of autumn sunshine in early October. Having originally decided to hand over the reins of Théâtre du Soleil to director Sylvain Creuzevault, she had just told him that she had changed her mind, that he would not be her successor after all. She blamed the troupe, that democratic, cosmopolitan group more involved than ever in the running of the theater and its productions. It was not yet official for anyone. The French Ministry of Culture, which had already given its approval, was furious. Wrapping herself in her sweater, ever alert, she confided that she had another lead, but that she could not reveal anything yet.
It is now official: Both the ministry and the troupe, recently affected by internal accusations of sexual assault and an audit of the theater's operations in the spring, have given their approval. Simon Abkarian has been chosen to succeed Mnouchkine. The actor and director has agreed to take on a challenge he had declined in 2022, when she first approached him. "It just wasn't the right time," he explained, now enthusiastic. "We will continue along the same path: popular, festive, accessible to everyone. The Soleil is an epic, political and philosophical theater. It's what made me who I am."

lemonde.fr/en.title: ECB: The new trio tasked with protecting Europe from inflation
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Remember these three names: If France is ever attacked on the financial markets and needs to be saved by the European Central Bank (ECB), they will be the first line of defense. On Thursday, November 26, the leaders of the 21 eurozone countries officially appointed the trio who will hold the monetary institution's most influential positions, European Council President António Costa announced. Pablo Hernández de Cos of Spain will succeed Christine Lagarde as president after she steps down on February 7, 2027, nine months before the end of her term. He will serve alongside French national Laurence Boone, who is set to take charge of the ECB's markets portfolio on January 4, 2027, succeeding Isabel Schnabel of Germany. Finally, German economist Markus Brunnermeier will become chief economist on June 1, 2027, replacing Philip Lane of Ireland.
This trio will make up half of the ECB's six-member executive board, which is based in the German city of Frankfurt am Main. They will be the most important members by far. Under the presidency of Italian Mario Draghi, Peter Praet, a Belgian national who oversaw economic policy, and Benoît Cœuré, who hailed from France and oversaw market operations, held the most influential posts. Under Lagarde, tensions between Philip Lane and Isabel Schnabel largely shaped the ECB's monetary policy, which tended to follow whichever one held the upper hand over the other at any given time.
The three newly appointed members are all well-known economists who have decades-long careers in central banking circles. Frederik Ducrozet, director of economic research at Pictet Wealth Management, described their appointment as a safe choice, warning that it risked leading to disappointment: "It's always a bit the same circle."

lemonde.fr/en.title: Marie-Antoinette's 'nipple bowl' auctioned for record $3.1 million
lemonde.fr/en.text:
A rare porcelain cup in the shape of a woman's breast, which once belonged to French Queen Marie-Antoinette, fetched a record €2.9 million ($3.1 million) at auction on Thursday, November 26.
Complete with a molded pink-tinged ceramic nipple, the late 18th-century masterpiece from the renowned Sèvres porcelain factory was thought lost for two centuries before its chance rediscovery in the inventory of the Meyer Gallery in Paris.
The jatte-teton, meaning nipple bowl, was one of four such pieces which King Louis XVI once ordered for Marie-Antoinette's dairy creamery at the royal residence in Rambouillet, southwest of the capital.
The Austrian-born royal was notorious for her extravagant spending, contributing to the souring of public opinion against the monarchy ahead of her execution by guillotine in October 1793 at the age of 37.
Hôtel Drouot, which auctioned off the shapely china, said the €2.9-million price was a record for a piece of Sèvres porcelain under the hammer. The auctioneer, which had estimated that the nipple bowl would sell between €1 and €2 million, did not reveal who had managed to get their hands on the extravagant piece.
Both Hôtel Drouot and the Coutau-Bégarie house, which organized the sale, decided to donate part of the auction's proceeds to the Pink Ribbon breast cancer charity.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Mélenchon heads to Berlin, where his anti-German rhetoric unsettles even his 'partners'
lemonde.fr/en.text:
The venue is symbolic: the Babylon cinema, with its iconic 1920s architecture, located on Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz. The site, in the heart of former East Berlin, next to the Berlin headquarters of the radical left-wing party Die Linke, is where Jean-Luc Mélenchon is slated to speak on Friday, November 27, during his trip to Berlin. The leftist French presidential candidate is to present the newly released German edition of his political theory book Now, the People!: Revolution in the 21st Century. According to his German publisher, more than 2,000 people have registered to attend the event.
The last time Mélenchon visited Berlin was in 2018, at the invitation of Die Linke, the distant successor of the former East German party SED. The party, which he calls "our German partner," even inspired the creation of his own movement, La France Insoumise (LFI), in 2016. This time, however, no meeting between the two parties has been confirmed so far. "Some [Die Linke] elected officials will attend the presentation on Friday evening," said LFI MP Hadrien Clouet, who is accompanying Mélenchon for his two-day visit to the German capital, on Friday and Saturday.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Emilie König, France's most high-profile female jihadist, faces justice
lemonde.fr/en.text:
Emilie König is, without a doubt, the most high-profile of the French female jihadists. The first encounter the woman from Brittany, now 41 years old, had with cameras dates back to the spring of 2012, one year before she left for Syria. At the time, she was 27 and had been wearing the niqab for two years.
The young woman from Lorient welcomed sociologist Agnès De Féo into her apartment. De Féo was conducting field research on the full-face veil in France and turned that encounter into a documentary, Emilie König vs Ummu Tawwab. In the film, the future jihadist, wearing black gloves and covered by a niqab (her "second skin," as she calls it), prepares pancakes while denouncing the rejection she said she experienced as a Muslim woman. "Emilie then appears to me to be seeking publicity, stepping in front of the camera," the sociologist wrote in an article published by Slate.
One year later, in June 2013, the young convert reappeared in the spotlight in a video, still covered in a niqab, firing a shotgun in an olive grove under the Syrian sun. The publicity-seeking Salafist militant had become a committed jihadist and a zealous propagandist for the Islamic State group (IS). On her Facebook account, she urged French people to join her, called on her "brothers" to kidnap and behead François Fillon, then prime minister, who was traveling in Iraq, and said she was "proud" to see IS's enemies "get beheaded or killed like common garbage": "It soothes my heart," she wrote.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Paris appeals court upholds trial order for Depardieu over rape claims
lemonde.fr/en.text:
A Paris appeal court on Thursday, November 26, upheld an order for actor and convicted sex offender Gérard Depardieu to stand trial on charges of raping fellow actor Charlotte Arnould, a judicial source said. Arnould has accused Depardieu of raping her twice in 2018 when she was 22 and suffering from anorexia.
Depardieu was charged in 2020 with rape and was ordered to stand trial in 2025, but the actor rejected the allegations and appealed. The court decided to uphold the order for a trial on rape and sexual assault charges, but only for part of the allegations.
The trial order was upheld "solely in relation to the events of the first day, August 7, 2018," the judicial source said, while the court "dismissed the allegations relating to August 13, 2018."
The 77-year-old actor has been the subject of multiple sexual assault accusations and charges in recent years. French police are investigating allegations that Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq gang-raped and assaulted a woman on camera during a 2018 film shoot. Last week, he dropped his appeal against an 18-month suspended sentence for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of another movie in 2021.
The Arnould decision "promises to be historic," according to her lawyer Carine Durrieu Diebolt. However, the actor's lawyer, David-Olivier Kaminski, told Agence France-Presse the decision marked an "initial victory for Gérard Depardieu." The actor could still appeal to the country's highest court.

lemonde.fr/en.title: Bardella's antisemitic messages: 19 elements proving he was the author, contrary to his denials
lemonde.fr/en.text:
When Mediapart revealed his antisemitic messages on September 28, Jordan Bardella, the president of Marine Le Pen's far-right Rassemblement National (RN), initially spoke of "a dirty trick," suggesting the investigative site was either the perpetrator or the victim. He became more vague in his denials after Mediapart published evidence three days later.
The incriminating Messenger conversation contains a wealth of evidence making it possible to state with certainty that Bardella was indeed the author of numerous antisemitic and conspiratorial statements. Some of these were previously revealed by Mediapart, and others can now be added. Through cross-checks, Le Monde has identified no fewer than 19 elements matching between the Jordan Bardella of the Messenger conversation and public statements he has made in the press, on Twitter (now X) and in his books.
Each element only reinforces the main piece of evidence: Our source, in the presence of Le Monde and a judicial officer, requested an archive of their 2013 conversations from Meta, which owns the Messenger app. The source, whom we are referring to as Sacha, showed the judicial officer their ID and entered their Facebook credentials. Twenty-four hours later, Sacha received a notification from Meta, the parent company of Facebook and Messenger, that their 2013 conversations had arrived in their account. Among them was a document titled "jordanbardella10207596331484581" containing their entire conversation with Bardella. It was an exact match of the conversation still visible on Sacha's phone.
Contacted by Le Monde, Bardella responded through his lawyer, Pascal Garbarini, that he was not the author of the incriminating remarks. The RN's president did not respond to questions on the numerous correlations.

welt.de.title: EU-Gipfel vorzeitig abgebrochen – Magyar macht sich über ergebnislose Verhandlungen lustig
welt.de.text: Nach stundenlangen und weitgehend ergebnislosen Haushaltsverhandlungen haben die Staats- und Regierungschefs der EU ihren Sondergipfel zur Finanzplanung bis 2034 vorzeitig beendet. Die Vorstellungen über Umfang und Verteilung der Finanzmittel würden noch „weit auseinanderliegen“, sagte  Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU)  am späten Abend. Man habe sich daher darauf verständigt, dass man das Treffen anders als ursprünglich geplant am Freitagvormittag nicht fortsetzen werde. Merz zeigte sich dennoch „zuversichtlich“, dass eine Einigung für einen mittelfristigen Finanzrahmen (MFR) bis zum Jahresende gelingen wird. Alle Mitgliedstaaten seien „darum bemüht, bis zum Ende des Jahres den Abschluss zu finden“, sagte er weiter. Der Kanzler verwies auf Wahlen in mehreren europäischen Staaten im kommenden Jahr, darunter in Frankreich, Italien und Polen. Die Wahlen machten es den amtierenden Staats- und Regierungschefs im kommenden Jahr nicht leichter, über den EU-Haushalt zu verhandeln, sagte Merz. Der EU-Haushalt könne „nicht unbegrenzt wachsen und die Lasten müssen auch fair verteilt sein“, wiederholte er. „Da sind wir noch nicht.“ Deutschland steht an der Spitze einer Gruppe „sparsamer“ Länder, die sich für eine nur mäßige Erhöhung des künftigen EU-Haushalts im Vergleich zum laufenden Budget einsetzen. „Wir dürfen auch in Europa keine Versprechungen machen, die wir nicht bezahlen können.“ Ratspräsident António Costa  beendete die Zusammenkunft, die am Morgen begonnen hatte, kurz nach Mitternacht. Er hatte den Gipfel für zwei Tage angesetzt, um die Verhandlungen über den nächsten langfristigen Haushalt endlich ein Stück weit voranzubringen – mangelnde Kompromissbereitschaft der Staats- und Regierungschefs machte ihm aber einen Strich durch die Rechnung. „Dieser Gipfel war ein notwendiger Schritt im Prozess“, verteidigte er sich anschließend. Merz und die anderen Staats- und Regierungschefs hatten sich auf einen Aufenthalt in Brüssel bis Freitagabend eingestellt. Der Kanzler hatte sogar schon mit der CDU/CSU-Fraktion im Bundestag abgemacht, dass er nicht zu der für Freitagnachmittag geplanten Abstimmung über den Bundeshaushalt 2027 in den Bundestag kommen muss. Jetzt kann er unverhofft doch noch dabei sein. Merz und Macron wollen nun Einigung im Dezember Ein Durchbruch war vor dem Gipfel ohnehin nicht erwartet worden, alle hatten sich von Anfang an darauf eingestellt, dass es erst bei einem weiteren Treffen im Dezember zum Showdown kommen werde. Sowohl  Frankreichs Präsident Emmanuel Macron  als auch Merz betonten aber, dass es dann zu einer Einigung kommen müsse. Macron hatte gewarnt, es wäre ein strategischer Fehler, den EU-Haushalt – so wie Merz es fordert – zu kürzen. Für den Fall, dass auch dieser Gipfel ohne Ergebnis bleibt, hat Frankreich angedroht, dass die Verhandlungen erst nach der für April angesetzten französischen Präsidentenwahl weitergehen würden. Die Wahl könnte nach derzeitigen Umfragen die EU-kritische Politikerin Marine Le Pen gewinnen, was eine Einigung wohl nochmals erschweren würde. Der  niederländische Regierungschef Rob Jetten  machte aber klar, dass er sich nicht hetzen lassen will. „Es gibt immer irgendein europäisches Land, in dem gerade gewählt wird“, sagte er. Ähnlich äußerte sich  Österreichs Kanzler Christian Stocker : „Ich habe hier keine Eile. Wenn die Bedingungen nicht stimmen, kann es auch keine Einigung geben.“ Wie andere Länder, die für Kürzungen plädieren, nahm auch Österreich nicht alle Einladungen zu den sogenannten Beichtstuhlgesprächen an, zu denen Costa Vertreter unterschiedlicher Gruppen einlud. Dies sei kein Boykott, betonte Stocker – und übte zugleich deutliche Kritik an der Verhandlungsführung des EU-Ratspräsidenten: „Für uns ist das ein Zeichen, dass wir mit der Art und Weise, wie der Prozess gestaltet ist, genauso wenig zufrieden sind wie mit dem Vorschlag, der vorgelegt wurde.“ Magyar hat zumindest etwas über Volleyball gelernt Ungarns Ministerpräsident Péter Magyar  machte sich auf X über die ergebnislosen Verhandlungen lustig. „Zumindest habe ich von der italienischen Ministerpräsidentin gelernt, dass ich meine Annahme beim Volleyball verbessern muss.“ Magyar hatte bei einem Besuch in der Ukraine gegen den ukrainischen Präsidenten Wolodymyr Selenskyj Volleyball gespielt, Aufnahmen davon machten schnell die Runde – offenbar auch bis nach Rom. Nach dem Gipfel schob Magyar hinterher, die Ratssitzung sei „völlig überflüssig“ gewesen. Die Mitgliedstaaten seien weiter voneinander entfernt als noch am Morgen, sagte er in der Nacht. Schon zu Beginn des Sondergipfels hatten mehrere Staats- und Regierungschefs deutlich gemacht, dass sie von ihren Positionen nicht abrücken wollen. Auf die Frage, ob es bei dem Sondergipfel überhaupt Fortschritte gegeben habe, sagte Merz: „Es gibt durchaus Bewegung Richtung weiterer Reduzierung dieser sogenannten Verhandlungsbox.“ Gemeint ist der Umfang des Gesamthaushalts, den Costa vor dem Gipfel um 204 auf 1.781 Milliarden Euro im Vergleich zum Kommissionsvorschlag reduziert hatte. „Das wird nicht bei 204 bleiben“, sagte Merz. Er verlangt eine weitere Kürzung um mehrere hundert Milliarden Euro und hat sich mit gleichgesinnten Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus den Nettozahler-Staaten Niederlande, Österreich, Schweden, Finnland, Dänemark und Belgien zusammengetan, um das durchzusetzen. Die Gruppe nennt sich „Die vernünftigen Sieben“ – „The sensible Seven“. Damit will sie deutlich machen, dass ein zu großer EU-Haushalt aus ihrer Sicht unvernünftig wäre. Ob aus den „Vernünftigen Sieben“ die „Glorreichen Sieben“ wie im gleichnamigen Western werden, wird sich im Dezember zeigen. Sie haben es mit einer großen Gruppe von Ländern zu tun, die keine weiteren Kürzungen wollen und hohe EU-Ausgaben für strukturschwache Regionen und die Landwirtschaft verteidigen. Viele dieser Staaten, vor allem in Süd- und Osteuropa, sind Nettoempfänger aus dem EU-Haushalt. Kritik kommt zudem von Ländern wie Frankreich und Italien, die auch Nettozahler sind, aber Einbußen für ihre Landwirte und Regionen vermeiden wollen. „Wir sind nicht bereit, unsere Unterschrift unter ein Budget zu setzen, in das wir mehr einzahlen, um weniger zu bekommen“, machte  Italiens Regierungschefin Giorgia Meloni  klar. Man sei noch „Lichtjahre“ von einer Einigung entfernt.

welt.de.title: „Hätte ihn gerne dabei“ – Trump würde Putin-Besuch bei G-20-Gipfel begrüßen
welt.de.text: US-Präsident Donald Trump würde eine Teilnahme des russischen Präsidenten Wladimir Putin am G-20-Gipfel im Dezember in Florida begrüßen. Er wisse zwar nicht, ob Putin anreisen werde, sagte Trump ‌am Donnerstag vor Journalisten auf seinem ‌Golfanwesen in Florida. „Wenn er kommen wollte, kann er das sicherlich tun.“ Einige Leute sähen Putin bei dem Treffen am 14. und 15. Dezember jedoch nicht gerne. Er bezweifle zudem, dass der russische Staatschef selbst teilnehmen wolle. „Wenn es nach mir ‌ginge, hätte ich ihn gerne dabei“, fügte Trump anlässlich des US-Feiertags Thanksgiving hinzu. Das Präsidialamt in Moskau teilte am Donnerstag mit, es sei noch keine Entscheidung über eine Teilnahme Putins gefallen. Der russische Präsident hatte nach einem Treffen mit Trump in der vergangenen ‌Woche erklärt, er werde eine Reise in die USA in Erwägung ‌ziehen, müsse dabei aber die Lage ‌in Russland berücksichtigen. Trump hatte zuvor auf seiner Online-Plattform Truth Social erklärt, er ‌würde es begrüßen, wenn Putin jegliche militärische Aggression gegen Gebiete in ganz Europa zurücknehme. Er äußerte die Hoffnung, dass dies zu einer raschen Beilegung des Krieges in der Ukraine führen könne.

welt.de.title: Schwerer Sturm in mehreren US-Staaten an Thanksgiving – Hunderttausende ohne Strom
welt.de.text: Ein schwerer Sturm hat in den USA am Feiertag Thanksgiving massive Stromausfälle und Verkehrsbehinderungen verursacht. Mehr als 900.000 Haushalte und Unternehmen waren am Donnerstag nach Angaben der Website PowerOutage ohne Strom. Besonders betroffen waren die östlichen Bundesstaaten Pennsylvania, Maryland und Virginia. Starkregen und heftige Winde trafen den Osten und die Mitte des Landes. Landesweit wurden der Website FlightAware zufolge knapp 400 Flüge gestrichen, mehr als 2000 weitere verspäteten sich. Entlang der Ostküste wurden Überschwemmungen gemeldet. Auch im Landesinneren stürzten wegen heftiger Windböen und aufgeweichter Böden Bäume auf Stromleitungen und Häuser. Mehrere wichtige Brücken wurden wegen des starken Winds gesperrt. Die Behörden riefen dazu auf, Autofahrten einzuschränken. In den Vororten der US-Hauptstadt Washington im Bundesstaat Maryland wurden aus Sorge vor Auswirkungen der Stromausfälle auf die Wasseraufbereitung knapp zwei Millionen Kunden aufgerufen, Leitungswasser zu sparen. Die Gouverneurin des Bundesstaats New Jersey, Mikie Sherrill, hatte bereits am Mittwoch den Notstand ausgerufen. „Halten Sie Ihre Geräte aufgeladen, melden Sie Stromausfälle direkt Ihrem Stromversorger und halten Sie sich von heruntergerissenen Stromleitungen fern“, schrieb sie im Onlinedienst X. In New York war die traditionelle Thanksgiving-Parade des Kaufhauses Macy's erstmals in ihrer hundertjährigen Geschichte verschoben worden. Sie soll nun am Samstag stattfinden. Auch an der US-Westküste hatten die Menschen in dieser Woche mit extremen Wetterbedingungen zu kämpfen. Gewaltige Wellen trafen auf die Küste Kaliforniens, in einigen Gebieten mussten Menschen in Sicherheit gebracht werden. Thanksgiving ist einer der wichtigsten Feiertage in den USA und traditionell ein Familienfest, zu dem meist Truthahn serviert wird. Rund um den Feiertag herrscht besonders reger Reiseverkehr.

welt.de.title: „Lichtjahre von Einigung entfernt“ – EU-Gipfel zum Billionen-Streit droht vorzeitiges Ende
welt.de.text: Wofür soll die EU künftig Geld ausgeben? Und welche Billionensumme braucht es? Im Streit um den nächsten langfristigen EU-Haushalt ist noch lange keine Einigung in Sicht. Beim EU-Gipfel versuchte Ratspräsident António Costa im sogenannten Beichtstuhlverfahren, die Differenzen zwischen den sehr unterschiedlichen Lagern zu verkleinern. Größere Fortschritte wurden trotz der Gespräche mit einzelnen Interessengruppen zunächst aber nicht sichtbar. Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz und die Gruppe der „Sensible Seven“ – die „Vernünftigen Sieben“ – pochten weiter auf einen harten Sparkurs. Trotz Costas jüngster Kürzung sei der Gesamtumfang von 1,78 Billionen Euro zu hoch, monierte der Kanzler zum Auftakt des Gipfels. „Europa braucht solide Finanzen.“ Merz forderte zudem eine klare Schwerpunktsetzung bei der Finanzplanung für die Jahre von 2028 bis Ende 2034. Priorität müssten Ausgaben für eine wettbewerbsfähige Wirtschaft und eine bessere Verteidigungsfähigkeit haben, erklärte er. Auch müsse dafür gesorgt werden, dass die Ukraine in den nächsten Jahren ausreichend unterstützt werde – und zwar von allen EU-Mitgliedern. „Lichtjahre von Einigung“ entfernt Kurz vor dem offiziellen Beginn des Gipfels hatte sich Merz zuvor mit ähnlich gesinnten Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus den Nettozahler-Staaten Niederlande, Österreich, Schweden, Finnland, Dänemark und Belgien getroffen. Die Gruppe nennt sich seit dem jüngsten Dazustoßen Belgiens „Die vernünftigen Sieben“. Damit will sie deutlich machen, dass ein zu großer EU-Haushalt aus ihrer Sicht unvernünftig wäre. Ihnen gegenüber steht eine große Gruppe von Ländern, die keine weiteren Kürzungen wollen und hohe EU-Ausgaben für strukturschwache Regionen und die Landwirtschaft verteidigen. Viele dieser Staaten, vor allem in Süd- und Osteuropa, sind Nettoempfänger aus dem EU-Haushalt. Kritik kommt zudem von Ländern wie Frankreich und Italien, die auch Nettozahler sind, aber Einbußen für ihre Landwirte und Regionen vermeiden wollen. „Wir sind nicht bereit, unsere Unterschrift unter ein Budget zu setzen, in das wir mehr einzahlen, um weniger zu bekommen“, machte Italiens Regierungschefin Meloni klar. Man sei noch „Lichtjahre von einer Einigung“ entfernt. Ähnlich äußerte sich Merz: Man stehe „in der Tat erst ganz am Anfang dieser Verhandlungen“. Die 27 Staats- und Regierungschefs berieten erst beim Mittagessen in großer Runde. Dann ging Costa in Gespräche mit kleineren Interessengruppen, um sie zu Zugeständnissen zu bewegen. Nach Angaben von EU-Diplomaten überlegt EU-Ratspräsident Costa, angesichts ​der Differenzen den zweitägigen Gipfel sogar zu verkürzen und ihn noch in der Nacht zu beenden. Merz setzt Abweichler bei Ukraine-Hilfe unter Druck Erschwert werden die Verhandlungen auch dadurch, dass Merz die Haushaltsverhandlungen zuletzt mit den Gesprächen über die Finanzierung neuer notwendiger Ukraine-Hilfen verknüpft hat. Er droht dabei mit einer Blockade, sollte die Ukraine-Finanzierung nicht von allen EU-Mitgliedern getragen werden. „Wenn die Europäische Union etwas finanziert, dann tut es die Europäische Union als Europäische Union“, sagte er. „Und zu dieser Europäischen Union gehören 27 und nicht 23 oder 24.“ Für 2027 hat die EU-Kommission zusätzliche Finanzhilfen für die Ukraine von bis zu 45 Milliarden Euro vorgeschlagen. Ungarn, die Slowakei und Tschechien wollen sich daran nicht beteiligen. Bulgarien zählte bisher auch zu den Abweichlern, hat sich aber inzwischen dazu bereiterklärt, humanitäre Hilfe zu leisten - aber keine militärische. Deutschland hat seit der russischen Invasion Anfang 2022 militärische und zivile Ukraine-Hilfe im Umfang von 100 Milliarden Euro geleistet oder in Aussicht gestellt und ist inzwischen der wichtigste Unterstützer weltweit. Die Unterstützung für die Ukraine-Hilfe in der Bevölkerung schwindet aber, wie mehrere Umfragen zeigen. Auch deswegen wirbt Merz vehement dafür, dass sich alle EU-Staaten beteiligen, damit die Ausgabenlast nicht weiter steigt. Ursprungsvorschlag schon einmal gekürzt Grundlage der aktuellen Gespräche ist ein am vergangenen Samstag vorgelegter Kompromissvorschlag von EU-Ratspräsident Costa. Er sieht vor, rund 204 Milliarden Euro weniger einzuplanen als bislang von der Europäischen Kommission vorgesehen. Nach dem Vorschlag Costas würde der nächste langfristige EU-Haushalt damit insgesamt rund 1,781 Billionen Euro umfassen. In absoluten Zahlen ist das deutlich mehr als im laufenden Finanzrahmen. Die nationalen Beiträge würden nach Costas Rechnung gemessen an der Wirtschaftsleistung jedoch kaum steigen. Um die Abflüsse aus den nationalen Haushalten nach Brüssel zu reduzieren, schlug Costa zudem die Einführung einer EU-weiten Digitalsteuer und einer Abgabe auf Krypto-Assets vor. Weitere Einnahmen sollen unter anderem aus dem Emissionshandel, dem CO2-Grenzausgleich CBAM, Tabak und nicht recyceltem Elektroschrott kommen. Nach Berechnungen Costas könnten die neuen Eigenmittel und Änderungen an bestehenden Einnahmequellen jährlich um die 60 Milliarden Euro zusätzlich einbringen. Erwartet wird, dass die Verhandlungen nach dem Spitzentreffen in dieser Woche auf Arbeitsebene bis zum Dezember-Gipfel kurz vor Weihnachten fortgesetzt werden. Bei diesem soll dann eine Einigung erzielt werden, um eine rechtzeitige Umsetzung zu ermöglichen. Für den Fall, dass der Gipfel scheitert, hat Frankreich angedroht, dass die Verhandlungen erst nach der für April angesetzten französischen Präsidentenwahl weitergehen würden. Die Wahl könnte nach derzeitigen Umfragen die EU-kritische Nationalistin Marine Le Pen gewinnen, was eine Einigung wohl nochmals erschweren würde.

welt.de.title: Kontrolle von Religionsgemeinschaften – Norwegen verschickt SMS an Millionen Bürger
welt.de.text: Norwegen verschickt ab kommender Woche SMS oder E-Mails an Millionen Menschen im Land, um deren Zugehörigkeit zu einer Glaubensgemeinschaft zu überprüfen. Damit verschärft die Regierung die Kontrollen, nachdem zahlreiche Fälle ans Licht gekommen waren, in denen Menschen ohne ihr Wissen als Mitglieder von Religionsgemeinschaften registriert wurden. „Die Menschen sollen selbst entscheiden können, wo sie Mitglied sein möchten“, sagte Kinder- und Familienministerin Lene Vågslid laut einer Mitteilung. „Und für falsch registrierte Mitgliedschaften sollen keine Zuschüsse gezahlt werden.“ Die SMS geht ab dem 30. November schrittweise an alle Einwohner raus, die mindestens 15 Jahre alt und als Mitglied einer Religionsgemeinschaft aufgeführt sind. Mit einem Link können die Betroffenen ihre Zugehörigkeit checken. Laut Medienberichten handelt es sich dabei um rund 3,5 bis 4 Millionen Menschen. Nach Angaben der norwegischen Nachrichtenagentur NTB kostet der Versand rund zwei Millionen norwegische Kronen. Die Nachrichten werden gestaffelt verschickt, um eine Überlastung der staatlichen Internetseite zu verhindern. Nach Angaben der Nachrichtenagentur NTB hatten zuvor mehr als 200 Menschen beim Staat Beschwerde eingelegt, nachdem sie entdeckt hatten, dass sie ohne ihr Zutun bei Religionsgemeinschaften registriert wurden. Mehr als 1000 Menschen haben die norwegische Zeitung „Verdens Gang“ demnach auf weitere Fälle hingewiesen. Die Hinweise betreffen laut NTB 180 verschiedene Glaubensgemeinschaften. Das entspricht mehr als einem Viertel der entsprechenden Gemeinschaften in Norwegen. Zuschuss pro Mitglied: 1611 Kronen Registrierte Religions- und Weltanschauungsgemeinschaften in Norwegen können einen jährlichen Zuschuss vom Staat bekommen, der sich nach der Zahl der Mitglieder richtet. Nach Angaben des norwegischen Familienministeriums beträgt dieser Zuschuss für Gemeinschaften außerhalb der norwegischen Kirche im Jahr 2026 grundsätzlich 1611 Kronen pro förderfähigem Mitglied. Werden fehlerhafte Mitgliedschaften festgestellt, können zu Unrecht ausgezahlte staatliche Zuschüsse zurückgefordert werden.

welt.de.title: Putin-Vertrauter Karaganow warnt – „Letztlich wird das in einem Atomkrieg enden“
welt.de.text: Bei einem Treffen mit BSW-Abgeordneten in Moskau hat der Putin-Vertraute Sergej Karaganow Europa mit dem Einsatz von Atomwaffen gedroht. „Wir sind bereit, den Krieg mit einem vollständigen Sieg Russlands über die Ukraine zu beenden“, sagte er gemäß einer Abschrift des Gesprächs, die der „ Zeit (verlinkt auf https://www.zeit.de/2026/51/bsw-michael-von-der-schulenburg-ruth-firmenich-sergej-karaganow-moskau) “ vorliegt. „Wenn nicht, werden wir weitermachen. Und letztlich wird das in einem Atomkrieg enden.“ Der 74-jährige Karaganow ist in Russland Ehrenvorsitzender des einflussreichen Rates für Außen- und Verteidigungspolitik. Ihm werden beste Drähte in den Kreml und zu Staatschef Wladimir Putin nachgesagt. Bereits im Juni waren die beiden Europa-Abgeordneten des Bündnis Soziale Gerechtigkeit und Wirtschaftliche Vernunft (BSW), Michael von der Schulenburg und Ruth Firmenich nach Moskau gereist, um für einen deutsch-russischen Dialog zu werben. Dabei trafen sie sich auch mit Karaganow. Das Gespräch wurde offenbar von russischer Seite aufgezeichnet, eine Abschrift liegt der Wochenzeitung nun vor. „Russland befindet sich derzeit in einer Position überlegener Stärke“ Karaganow bestritt die Echtheit der Zitate aus dem Gespräch in einer E-Mail an die „Zeit“ nicht. Während des Gesprächs sagte er laut der Abschrift: „Russland befindet sich derzeit in einer Position überlegener Stärke. Wenn jemand in Deutschland normale Beziehungen herstellen möchte, bin ich bereit, ihn zu unterstützen.“ Aber Russland werde dabei „nicht als Bittsteller auftreten“, so Karaganow. Schließlich verhielten sich die europäischen Regierungen seiner Meinung nach wie „Idioten und Revanchisten“. Bei dem Treffen stellte der Europa-Abgeordnete von der Schulenburg sich und Firmenich laut der Abschrift als „Freunde Russlands“ vor. Die beiden Abgeordneten wollten einen Dialog „unterhalb der Regierungsebene“ organisieren, wie von der Schulenburg laut Abschrift gesagt hat. Ziel eines solchen Gesprächsformats soll es sein, die deutsch-russischen Beziehungen zu verbessern und ein Ausweiten des Krieges zu verhindern.

welt.de.title: „27 und nicht 23 oder 24“ – Merz dringt auf Beteiligung aller EU-Länder an Ukraine-Hilfe
welt.de.text: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz (CDU) hat beim EU-Gipfel in Brüssel erneut auf eine Beteiligung aller EU-Staaten an den Hilfen für die Ukraine gedrungen. Die Finanzierung Kiews sei „eine Aufgabe, die wir auch gemeinsam leisten müssen“, sagte Merz am Donnerstag. Zur Europäischen Union „gehören 27 und nicht 23 oder 24“, mahnte er. Bislang gibt es eine Ausnahme bei den Ukraine-Hilfen für die Slowakei, Tschechien und Ungarn. Die drei Länder hatten für den laufenden 90-Milliarden-Euro-Kredit für Kiew ausgehandelt, dass sie sich an der Absicherung des Darlehens nicht beteiligen müssen. Österreichs Bundeskanzler Christian Stocker stellte sich hinter Merz’ Forderung. „Wir brauchen eine gemeinschaftliche Lösung“, sagte er in Brüssel. Ausnahmen wie bislang könnten „in Zukunft kein Weg mehr sein“. Es brauche eine „andere Vorgehensweise“. Merz hat die Finanzierung der Ukraine an seine Zustimmung zum nächsten mehrjährigen Haushalt der EU geknüpft, über den in Brüssel bei dem Gipfel am Donnerstag und Freitag verhandelt wird. Erklärtes Ziel ist eine Einigung zu beiden Themen im Dezember. Der tschechische Regierungschef Andrej Babis widersprach dem deutschen Kanzler. „Die Finanzierung der Ukraine sollte separat verhandelt werden“, forderte er. Sein Land brauche das Geld für andere Ausgaben. „Ich glaube, wir werden um dieses Geld kämpfen.“ Die Verhandlungen um den mehrjährigen Finanzrahmen der EU für die Jahre 2028 bis 2034 schienen zuletzt festgefahren. Ein Gipfel im Oktober hatte keine Ergebnisse gebracht. Der jetzige Sondergipfel soll eine erste Annäherung zwischen den Lagern der als die „Sparsamen“ bezeichneten Staaten wie Deutschland und Österreich und den „Freunden der Kohäsion“ bringen. Diese Staaten plädieren für einen großen Haushalt, der wie bisher auch den Schwerpunkt auf Agrar- und Regionalförderung legen soll.
